page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-176 is an enterprise-scale instance powered by 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Emerald Rapids / Sapphire Rapids 8481C) running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The machine provides 176 dedicated virtual CPUs across 88 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 105 MB of shared L3 cache. With a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU, the instance includes 1408 GB of total system RAM, aligning it firmly with large-scale in-memory compute requirements.

The x86_64 processor architecture includes extensive instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like VAES and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and does not bundle local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent storage must be attached over the network via Cloud Storage or Persistent Disk volumes.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier parallel execution and memory throughput. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 146,417.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 104,670.37, while single-core processing scores in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench. Large block memory read throughput peaks at 446.56 GB/s, while write operations reach 195.8 GB/s. High memory speed and core count drive exceptional throughput in in-memory workloads, demonstrated by 164.09 million Redis SET operations per second and 122.92 GB/s in static web serving benchmarks.

Given its massive scale and dedicated resource profile, the instance offers strong resource density for organizations consolidating distributed jobs into a single NUMA-aware footprint. Tradeoffs include average single-threaded performance and dependence on remote block storage. It is primarily suited for large in-memory databases like Redis or SAP HANA, distributed data processing engines, massive batch compilation pipelines, and memory-bound scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-176 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 176 dedicated vCPUs (88 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz and 1408 GB of RAM. Designed for high memory-to-compute ratios of 8.0 GB per vCPU, the configuration supports hardware extensions including AVX-512 and AMX for specialized arithmetic. It operates without discrete GPUs or local disk storage, relying on network-attached persistence. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional multithreaded capacity, delivering a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 146,417.7 and 164.09 million Redis operations per second, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 446.56 GB/s. While single-thread benchmarks remain in the mid-range, the instance delivers high compute and memory density for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, parallel software builds, and heavy enterprise workloads.
